newsitem.title: USA: Pittway Penton unit buys trade show firm.
newsitem.headline: Pittway Penton unit buys trade show firm.

text.p: Pittway Corp's Penton Publishing trade magazine unit said Thursday it has acquired A/E/C Systems International Inc, a trade show company.

"The acquisition of A/E/C Sytems fits our overall strategy to increase Penton's portfolio of trade shows and conferences and to expand our position in our current market segments with an array of media properties," Penton chairman and chief executive officer Tom Kemp said in a statement.
Cleveland-based Penton publishes Industry Week and about 90 other magazines and owns five other trade shows.
A/E/C, based in Exton, Pa., will be a Penton division but retain its name, and its founders, George Borkovich and Michael Hough, will remain with the company, Penton said.
A/E/C's trade shows feature computer technology applications for the architecture, engineering and building industries. It also publishes Computer Solutions magazine.
Penton magazines include Computer-Aided Engineering, Machine Design and Heating/Piping/Air-Conditioning. Penton revenues are about $200 million a year, it said.
Chicago-based Pittway manufactures and distributes professional burglar and fire alarm equipment.
